newRun.evaluationHelp: The run measures the loss on examples it does not train on, about ten times over the run.
newRun.advancedHelp: Hardware is auto mode's choice: the plan job asks for the base model's 16-bit weights plus 8 GB, the training job for the memory Meep²'s plan states, and the node gives its default CPU cores.
newRun.setHardware: Set the jobs' memory and CPU cores myself
newRun.milestonesHelp: Keep the adapter at a share of the training and, with an evaluation set, score what the model writes at each one.
newRun.milestoneGroupHelp: Each value is scored apart, such as a translation direction.
newRun.milestoneSourceHelp: The source alone, without the instruction: an answer is cut at twice its tokens + 32. Without it, the prompt's last message counts.
newRun.milestoneMetricsHelp: The scoring service's metrics, separated by commas.

chat.loadFirst: Serve at least one of the two models to ask it.

export.title: Export to GGUF
export.help: Convert the registered model to a GGUF file with llama.cpp's converter. The LLM Gateway serves it on llama.cpp, and Ollama and other llama.cpp tools read it. The conversion needs no GPU.
export.running: Converting and uploading; this takes some minutes.
export.done: {{id}} is in the model catalogue, served by llama.cpp.

slots.title: Slots
slots.subtitle: A slot is a node and a recurring time window in which it trains. Outside its slots the node serves models and runs apps as usual.
slots.loadFailed: The slots could not be loaded
slots.worker: The queue's access to Thinkube Control
slots.workerHelp: The queue starts notebook jobs and turns training mode on and off when nobody is signed in. For that it keeps a Thinkube Control API token of the person who connects it, and acts with that person's rights.
slots.disconnectConfirm: The token is revoked in Thinkube Control. The queue starts nothing until it is connected again; running trainings go on.
slots.listHelp: At a slot's start, training mode is turned on for its node: its served models are unloaded and its other workloads stop. At its end, the running training pauses with a checkpoint, and the node comes back as it was.
slots.none: No slots yet. Runs queued for slots wait until their node has one.
slots.overlapRule: Training mode reserves one node at a time. When runs on two nodes want it, the run with the higher priority takes it first; at equal priority, the slot that started first. The other waits until it ends, and starts then if its slot is still open.
slots.addHelp: The days are the days the window starts on.
slots.endHelp: An end before the start is on the next day. An end equal to the start is a whole day.
slots.deleteConfirm: If the slot is open now, its runs pause at once.

priority.title: Priority
priority.runHelp: 1 is the highest. Work on the node with a higher or the same priority makes the run wait; work with a lower one is stopped to make room.
priority.subtitle: Every piece of work on a GPU node has a priority, from 1 (highest) to 5 (lowest). Forge runs have their own; the rest have the priority of their kind, set here.
priority.ruleHelp: When a run wants its node: work with a higher priority makes it wait, and work with the same priority too; work with a lower priority is stopped to make room, in the gentlest way it has. This holds at any time: a run of priority 1 added later stops a running run of priority 3.

kinds.forge_run: Forge runs (the priority a new run gets)

stop.forge_run: Paused at its next step with a checkpoint; the queue resumes it later.
stop.served_model: Unloaded by training mode, and loaded again when it ends.
stop.app: Scaled to 0 by training mode, and restored when it ends.

priority.trainingMode: Training mode reserves one node at a time. When runs on two nodes want it, the one with the higher priority takes it first; the other waits until it ends. A run does not take training mode from another node, whatever its priority.

nvfp4.title: Export to NVFP4
nvfp4.help: Quantize the registered model to NVFP4 with NVIDIA's TensorRT Model Optimizer, calibrated on rows of the split the run trained on, and publish it for vLLM. NVFP4 is computed by Blackwell GPUs (compute capability 10.0 and higher), such as the DGX Spark; the gateway serves it only there.
nvfp4.noNode: No GPU node of the cluster computes NVFP4: it needs compute capability 10.0 or higher.
nvfp4.rowsHelp: Drawn with a fixed seed from the split the run trained on.
nvfp4.running: Calibrating, quantizing and uploading; this takes some minutes.
nvfp4.done: {{id}} is in the model catalogue, served by vLLM on Blackwell GPUs.
